problem: What is the projection of the intersection between the sphere $(x-1)^{2}+(y-6)^{2}+{z}^{2}=17$ and the plane $y=5$ onto the $xz$-plane.
worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the sphere and the plane $y=5$, we substitute $y=5$ into the equation of the sphere:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2}+(5-6)^{2}+{z}^{2} & =17 \\ (x-1)^{2}+1+{z}^{2} & =17 \\ (x-1)^{2}+{z}^{2} & =16 \\ (x-1)^{2}+{z}^{2} & ={4}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Projecting this onto the $xz$-plane gives us the equation of the circle of radius $4$ centered at $(1,0).$
